questions.prompt: What is the difference between routing and forwarding?

options.text: Routing builds the map of best next hops; forwarding moves each packet using it
Routing moves packets; forwarding builds the table
Forwarding only happens on the client, routing only on servers

questions.explanation: Routing (control plane) builds the routing table; forwarding (data plane) uses it to move each packet to its next hop.

questions.prompt: A packet to 10.0.5.20 matches routes 0.0.0.0/0, 10.0.0.0/8, and 10.0.5.0/24. Which is used?
questions.explanation: Longest-prefix match wins: /24 is more specific than /8 or /0, so the 10.0.5.0/24 route is chosen.

questions.prompt: The catch-all route used when no more specific route matches is written as ____.
questions.explanation: 0.0.0.0/0 is the default route — everything not matched by a more specific prefix follows it.

questions.prompt: Which statements about internet routing are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: IP delivery is hop-by-hop and best-effort
BGP routes between autonomous systems and is policy-driven
OSPF is an interior gateway protocol used within one network
There is a single global planner that computes each packet's full path

questions.explanation: Delivery is hop-by-hop, BGP is the policy-driven exterior protocol, and OSPF is interior. No global planner exists — each router decides locally.

questions.prompt: Match each routing term to its description.

pairs.right: A network under one administrative control

questions.explanation: The table maps prefixes to next hops, an AS is one admin domain, OSPF is interior, and BGP is the exterior protocol.

questions.prompt: Order what a router does with an arriving packet.

items.text: Look up the destination in the routing table
Forward out the interface toward the next hop

questions.explanation: The router looks up the destination, picks the most specific route, decrements TTL, and forwards to the next hop.
